title: Bower Privacy Profile
description: Privacy profile for the Privacy & Secret Protection Engine (kind: PrivacyProfile). Editor support only: the loader is authoritative and also rejects unknown keys, invalid custom detector patterns and failing custom detector tests.

action.description: Privacy action. Case-insensitive; hyphens are ignored (alert-only = AlertOnly). hmac needs a host HMAC key; encrypt without a 32-byte key removes the value.

customDetectorId.description: Custom detector id: custom.<name>, lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters.

customDetector.description: Custom detector (custom redaction rule): a restricted, deterministic pattern applied wherever built-in value detectors run (string and number values, property names).

pattern.description: Restricted syntax: literals, escaped punctuation, \t \n \r, \d \w \s (ASCII) and negations, ., classes and ranges, (...) and (?:...), * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} (bounds at most 1000) with optional lazy ?, |, ^ and $ (whole value). No lookaround, back-references, inline flags, named groups, \b, \p{...} or other escapes. Expansion estimate at most 512; must not match an empty string.

ignoreCase.description: ASCII letters only; non-ASCII letters stay case-sensitive.

wholeWord.description: Keep a match only when the characters around it are not ASCII letters, digits or underscore.

tests.description: Checked at load: every match sample must match and no noMatch sample may match (after wholeWord filtering).

fieldRule.description: Deterministic action on a dot-separated JSON path from the event root; * matches one segment.

detectors.description: Built-in detector action overrides. Custom detectors set their action in customDetectors.

disabled.description: Built-in or custom detector ids to switch off.

enableOptIn.description: Opt-in built-in detectors to switch on (custom detectors are always on unless disabled).

secretFieldNames.description: Extra field names removed like built-in field-name secrets. Compared after normalisation (letters and digits only, lower-cased), so sessionKey also covers session_key and SESSION-KEY.
